# Draft:Wispr Flow (Voice Dictation Software)

Wispr Flow is a voice dictation software application developed by Wispr, Inc. that provides real-time speech-to-text transcription capabilities. First released for macOS in September 2024 and later expanded to Windows in March 2025, the software utilizes speech recognition technology to convert spoken language into written text across various applications and platforms, offering an alternative to keyboard-based text input.
Technology
Wispr Flow processes audio input and converts it to text output in real-time. The technology allows users to dictate text in various contexts without changing their workflow. Voice recognition represents an alternative approach to human-computer interaction compared to traditional text input methods and can be particularly beneficial for accessibility purposes, allowing individuals with mobility limitations to interact with computers more effectively.
History
Wispr Flow was developed by Wispr, Inc., a technology company founded in 2021 by Tanay Kothari and Sahaj Garg in San Francisco, California. The company focuses on creating natural user interfaces for technology interaction.
The development of Wispr Flow was supported by several funding rounds. In September 2024, the company secured $12 million in investment capital, bringing their total funding to $26 million..This funding round was led by Matt Kraning, Chief Technology Officer of Cortex at Palo Alto Networks, with participation from NEA, 8VC, Tim Junio (founder and former CEO of Expanse), and Alumni Ventures.
The company has announced plans for an iOS version of the software. Both the macOS and Windows versions received "Product of the Day" recognition on Product Hunt, indicating significant user interest.
